chapter_name: Physical Education Relation with other Subjects
learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how Physical Education isn't just about playing games—it's deeply connected to science, math, psychology, and sociology!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Physical Education (PE) doesn't exist in isolation. It borrows concepts from biology, physics, psychology, and history to optimize human performance and health.
Physics explains how we move. Concepts like force, friction, velocity, and gravity help athletes run faster, jump higher, and throw farther without injury.
To train effectively, we must understand the human body—how muscles contract, how the heart pumps oxygen, and how bones provide leverage.
Sports are 90% mental! Psychology helps athletes deal with pressure, build motivation, set goals, and develop a winning mindset.
Sports bring people together. It teaches teamwork, leadership, fair play, and helps bridge cultural and social gaps.

fun_activity.title: 📐 The Math of a Throw
fun_activity.instructions: Take a ball and throw it at different angles. A throw at exactly 45 degrees usually goes the farthest. You just used Physics and Math in Physical Education!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly define 'Biomechanics' and give an example (like the angle of a javelin throw).
📌 Be ready to explain how psychology improves sports performance (managing anxiety, increasing focus).
📌 Remember that Anatomy is the study of structure, and Physiology is the study of function.
quick_recap: ⭐ Physical education relies heavily on the laws of physics to improve sports techniques.
⭐ Understanding human biology prevents sports injuries.
⭐ Sports sociology studies how sports influence culture and society.
